data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA 2022 Volume III report summarises results on creative thinking and related policy-relevant patterns alongside broader performance and equity themes. It reports that nearly 700 000 15-year-old students from 81 OECD member and partner economies participated in PISA 2022, and it highlights cross-country differences in mathematics performance trends since 2018, including declines in reading and mathematics and variation in low performance shares. The volume also describes relationships between students’ reported technology use, teacher support, parental engagement, and mathematics performance, including examples of systems maintaining or improving performance and systems showing large shares of students reaching basic proficiency. The excerpt does not provide the specific analytic model forms, PV-combining rules, missing-data strategy, or any machine-learning training/evaluation details, so the findings should be interpreted as descriptive and correlational within PISA’s standard scaling and reporting framework.
